Subject: Post-call: Tool-calling integration patterns and next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align teams.

Recap of the call (high level):
- Primary use-case: interactive agent that calls internal FinApps services (payments, ledger queries, customer profile lookup) and returns structured responses into the UI.
- Priorities: low-latency lookups for balances, safe/controlled tool invocation, and reranking of candidate answers using embeddings.
- Constraints: must support OAuth-based SSO for user-scoped calls, audit logging, and the ability to fallback to a read-only model when downstream tools are unavailable.

Key integration/architecture patterns we discussed:
1) SDK + Auth: Redwood SDK in the frontend/backend for streaming responses; recommended pattern is short-lived service tokens for server-side calls and OAuth for user-scoped tool calls.
2) Tool definitions: declare tools in the model call with explicit input/output schemas to enable structured output + validation.
3) Routing & fallbacks: route to primary tool endpoints with automatic fallback to cached or read-only endpoints; model variant fallback for degraded capacity.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: embed candidate documents, run cosine similarity filter, then rerank with lightweight model scoring before final output.

Attachments: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (patterns + examples), auth-patterns-cheatsheet.pdf (OAuth vs API key flow), architecture-diagram.png (proposed routing).

Proposed next steps:
- Dev deep-dive: schedule 60m technical session with FinApps infra and our infra team to go through SDK integration patterns and auth flow (Dev / Aditya + your infra).
- Demo: 30m demo of a tool-calling flow (structured output + embeddings reranker) using a FinApps-simulated dataset.
- Security checklist: share initial list of audit/logging requirements and sample SOC2 evidence we can provide.

Suggested times (PST): Wed 3/4 10:00am, Wed 3/4 2:00pm, Thu 3/5 11:00am — pick one and we’ll lock it.

Thanks — I’ll hold a calendar invite once you confirm.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Tool-calling integration patterns and next steps — technical notes

Alex / Priya — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive. I’ll take the 60m session with your infra folks and walk through these patterns.

1) Auth/token lifecycle
- Recommendation: Use OIDC for user-scoped tool calls. Sequence: user signs in via SSO -> exchange code for short-lived access token (1 hour) + refresh token stored server-side. For server-to-server calls use short-lived service tokens (rotate via KMS); we support automatic rotation in the SDK.
- Refresh pattern: Redwood SDK exposes a tokenProvider callback so you can centralize refresh logic; if a tool call returns 401 we trigger a refresh attempt and retry once.

2) Tool definitions & multi-step flows
- Best practice: model-invoked tools should be small, idempotent primitives (e.g., GET_BALANCE, INIT_PAYMENT, CONFIRM_PAYMENT). For multi-step flows we recommend:
  a) Orchestrate complex business logic server-side (transactional guarantees, retries, compensation).
  b) Use model-invoked tools for side-effects that are quick and safe (e.g., lookup, pre-check).
- Example tool definition (JSON schema style) included in the attached PDF. Key points:
  - name: string
  - inputs: {schema as JSON Schema string}
  - outputs: {schema}
  - timeout_ms, retry_policy, auth_scope

3) Routing & parallel tools
- Parallel tool calls: SDK can fan-out in parallel to multiple tool endpoints and return a merged structured response. We recommend an aggregator component server-side that:
  - launches parallel requests (payments, ledger lookup, risk check) with per-call timeouts
  - collects successes, scores them (confidence), and returns structured payload to the model for final synthesis
- If a tool is critical, mark it as "blocking"; otherwise mark as "best-effort" so model can produce a degraded-but-safe response.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- You can:
  a) Host embeddings in your index and expose a private endpoint Redwood calls for retrieval (we support VPC/Private networking).
  b) Push embeddings to Redwood (encrypted at rest) for lower latency if you want Redwood to do reranking server-side.
- Typical pattern: filter by embedding similarity first (top N), then do a rerank using a small scoring model. We provide a rerank API pattern in the PDF attached.

5) Error handling & observability
- Retry best-practices: exponential backoff + jitter, per-tool max attempts. For user-facing flows, use idempotency keys for side-effecting calls.
- Observability: include trace IDs in every tool call. Redwood will surface per-token latency and per-tool call metrics in Console so you can set SLOs.

6) Sample snippet (pseudo):
- Tool declaration (JS):
  const tools = [
    { name: 'GET_BALANCE', inputSchema: {...}, outputSchema: {...}, authScope: 'account.read' },
    { name: 'INIT_PAYMENT', inputSchema: {...}, outputSchema: {...}, authScope: 'payments.write' },
  ];

- Parallel call pattern:
  const results = await Promise.allSettled([callGET(), callRisk(), callLedger()]);
  const successes = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').map(r => r.value);

I’ll bring example code and the architecture slide to the session. If you want, I can also prepare an end-to-end demo that hits a sandboxed FinApps API (we can use mutual TLS or a signed JWT for the demo).
